item.title: Heron Fountain - principal was created by Heron of Alexandria in the 1st century
item.description: Hero of Alexandria also known as Heron of Alexandria probably 1st or 2nd century AD) was a Greek mathematician and engineer who was active in Alexandria during the Roman era. He has been described as the greatest experimentalist of antiquity and a representative of the Hellenistic scientific tradition Heron studied the pressure of air and steam, described the first steam engine, and built toys that would spurt water, one of them known as Heron's fountain. Various versions of Heron's fountain are used today in physics classes as a demonstration of principles of hydraulics and pneumatics.

Dr. Joel Bervell is an award winning medical doctor, medical mythbuster, science communicator, and advocate of iterating modern medical practices.

item.title: Here are the 50 live sites showing what’s happening in the world, organized by category
item.description: ### #Weather, #Climate & Oceans 1. **ventusky.com** → Interactive map of weather, precipitation, wind and waves 2. **earth.nullschool.net** → Global wind, ocean currents and pollution 3. **climatereanalyzer.org** → Real-time temperature anomalies 4. **nhc.noaa.gov** → Official hurricane tracking center (NOAA) 5. **tropicaltidbits.com** → Storm models side by side 6. **tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov** → Tides and water levels 7. **waterdata.usgs.gov** → Real-time river flow 8. **droughtmonitor.unl.edu** → Drought monitoring map ### Fires, Smoke & Air Quality 9. **firms.modaps.eosdis.nasa.gov** → Active fires by satellite (NASA) 10. **fire.airnow.gov** → Smoke plume tracking 11. **aqicn.org** / **waqi.info** → Real-time air quality in cities ### Satellites, #Earth Imagery & Observation 12. **worldview.earthdata.nasa.gov** → Daily global satellite imagery (NASA) 13. **sentinel-hub.com** → Explore Sentinel satellite images 14. **nsidc.org** → Polar ice and glacier status 15. **sealevel.nasa.gov** → Sea-level change data ### #Volcanos, Earthquakes & Tsunamis 16. **volcanodiscovery.com** → Real-time volcanic activity 17. **volcano.si.edu** → Active volcanoes database 18. **emsc-csem.org** / **seismicportal.eu** → Earthquake monitoring 19. **raspberryshake.net** → Listen to seismometers live 20. **tsunami.gov** → Tsunami warning center ### Space, Auroras & Celestial Objects 21. **aurora-service.eu** → Aurora forecasts 22. **spaceweather.com** / **swpc.noaa.gov** → Space weather and solar storms 23. **heavens-above.com** / **n2yo.com** / **spotthestation.nasa.gov** → Satellite and ISS tracking 24. **theskylive.com** / **solarsystemscope.com** → Planet positions and solar system 25. **cneos.jpl.nasa.gov** → Near-Earth objects 26. **fireball.amsmeteors.org** → Meteor and fireball reports 27. **suncalc.org** → Sun path during the day 28. **lightpollutionmap.info** → Dark-sky regions ### Aviation, Traffic & Transport 29. **adsbexchange.com** / **opensky-network.org** → Live flight tracking (unfiltered / open data) 30. **openrailwaymap.org** → Worldwide railway network ### Energy & Infrastructure 31. **electricitymaps.com** → Real-time electricity mix by country 32. **energy-charts.info** → European energy production data 33. **gridwatch.co.uk** → Live UK power grid load 34. **netblocks.org** / **radar.cloudflare.com** → Internet outages and traffic ### Oceans, Animals & Biodiversity 35. **ocearch.org** → Shark tracking 36. **globalfishingwatch.org** → Global fishing fleet monitoring 37. **birdcast.info** / **ebird.org** → Bird migration and observations 38. **movebank.org** → Animal migration routes 39. **inaturalist.org** / **gbif.org** → Live biodiversity observations ### Radio & Other 40. **websdr.org** → Listen to radio receivers around the world Most of these sites remain active and reliable. They use official data from NASA, NOAA, ESA and other scientific organizations, with updates ranging from near real-time to a few hours.

item.title: GovBrief Today #593
item.description: Donald Trump's Pentagon stopped answering questions about his war, so the troops and the accountants answered for him. The Congressional Budget Office says the Iran war has cost $38 billion through August 1, and it noted the Defense Department refused to answer its questions. The report found the war has used at least half of the missile interceptors the country keeps for a fight with China, and replacing them will take at least five years. Active-duty service members went further. They sent CBS News photos the Pentagon never showed the public, a destroyed radar plane in Saudi Arabia and burned-out barracks in Kuwait. Trump called the war "small potatoes" last week. One of the soldiers who sent the photos put it differently: "We're standing there with our eyes closed getting punched in the face." item.title: Dallas using AI cameras on garbage trucks to make sure your grass is cut.
item.description: Garbage Trucks Now Have AI Cameras To Score Your House and Clock Code Violations by Andrew P. Collins September 15 at 1:06 PM The city of Dallas, Texas, armed its trash collection trucks with AI-powered cameras earlier this year. This month, the NBC station down there did an investigation and discovered that they’re being used to assign “blight scores” to homes and send residents warning letters about things like grass height and dirty chimneys. Basically, we now have the technology to turn the entire country into an HOA. I’m sick of writing about the horrors of automated infrastructure, but this nonsense needs to be stopped before it spreads. NBC 5 Investigates found that “artificial intelligence identified at least one possible code violation on more than 21,000 properties,” and then shared some examples of things that were flagged: “Lawn, Grass Height, Sidewalk, Debris.” The station caught up with local real estate broker Ty Williams, who got a courtesy notice for “chimney paint” on a house he owned after one of these cameras came by. He shared a photo of the chimney, and it’s, like, just a regular chimney with some slight discoloration from age. “It’s a money grab. That’s basically what this is all about,” Williams said to NBC. No kidding. And, obviously, any operation to judge citizens on the tidiness of their front yards disproportionately screws lower- and fixed-income folks. Not everybody can afford the time and money to have their place manicured for trash collection day every week. The company that operates the cameras is called City Detect, and its tendrils extend way beyond Dallas. The City Detect tech is working in at least three other states besides Texas. NBC shared a statement from the company’s CEO: “Our system blurs faces and license plates, doesn’t connect to any law enforcement or federal database, and, by design, requires city staff to review a detection before any action is taken.” There’s not much comfort one can take from that. Not “connected to a federal database” doesn’t mean it can’t be used for nefarious purposes (intentionally or unintentionally). And that doesn’t get at the immediate problem: This tech effectively creates a new tax on people who are unable to bring their property to somebody’s beauty standards in time for trash day. This kind of thing is going to continue to be a problem unless, maybe, we complain about it relentlessly. In Dallas, City Council member Chad West proposed a budget amendment “that would strip funding for the cameras,” but it got delayed. West agreed to table his request after he said the city manager agreed to a hearing on the issue in December. For the rest of us, here’s a new technology to be informed about and vote against every chance you get. Full story: https://apple.news/AI5cQRl0wTWa4mq0Oy-jlKQ
